text: Which of the following processes is $\text{Anaerobic}$?
image: [Diagram comparing aerobic and anaerobic respiration pathways]
explanation: Fermentation (e.g., Lactic $\text{Acid}$ or $\text{Alcoholic}$) is a metabolic process that occurs in the $\text{Absence}$ of $\text{Oxygen}$, regenerating $\text{NAD}^+$ needed for $\text{Glycolysis}$ to continue.

text: The $\text{Chromosome}$ number in the $\text{Gametes}$ of a human is:
image: [Diagram showing human karyotype and gamete formation]
explanation: Gametes (sperm and egg) are $\text{Haploid}$ ($	ext{n}$), meaning they contain $\text{Half}$ the number of chromosomes found in somatic (body) cells. Human somatic cells are $\text{Diploid}$ ($	ext{2n} = 46$), so gametes have $\text{n} = 23$ chromosomes.

text: In $\text{Humans}$, the $\text{Sex}$-$\text{Linked}$ condition resulting from the $\text{Inability}$ of the $\text{Blood}$ to $\text{Clot}$ is:
explanation: $\text{Haemophilia}$ is a $\text{Recessive}$ $\text{Disorder}$ where blood doesn't $\text{Clot}$ normally due to a lack of $\text{Clotting}$ $\text{Factors}$. It is carried on the $\text{X}$ $\text{Chromosome}$ (sex-linked).

text: The $\text{Organelle}$ primarily responsible for $\text{Detoxification}$ of $\text{Metabolic}$ $\text{Wastes}$ and $\text{Drugs}$ in the $\text{Liver}$ cells is the:
image: [Diagram of a eukaryotic cell highlighting the Endoplasmic Reticulum]
explanation: The $\text{Smooth}$ $\text{ER}$ plays a $\text{Key}$ $\text{Role}$ in the $\text{Synthesis}$ of $\text{Lipids}$ and $\text{Steroids}$, and critically, the $\text{Metabolism}$ and $\text{Detoxification}$ of $\text{Drugs}$ and $\text{Poisons}$ in the $\text{Liver}$.

text: A $\text{Food}$ $\text{Chain}$ always begins with a:
image: [Diagram illustrating a simple food chain (producer -> primary consumer -> secondary consumer)]
explanation: $\text{Producers}$ (e.g., $\text{Plants}$ and $\text{Algae}$) are $\text{Autotrophs}$ that $\text{Create}$ their $\text{Own}$ $\text{Food}$ (usually through $\text{Photosynthesis}$) and form the $\text{Base}$ of every $\text{Food}$ $\text{Chain}$.

text: Which of these is $\text{NOT}$ a $\text{Characteristic}$ of $\text{Insects}$?
image: [Diagram of an insect showing 3 body parts and 6 legs]
explanation: Insects are characterized by having $\text{Three}$ $\text{Pairs}$ of $\text{Legs}$ ($	ext{6}$ legs) attached to the $\text{Thorax}$. $\text{Arachnids}$ (Spiders, Scorpions) have four pairs of legs.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Periodic}$ $\text{Shedding}$ of the $\text{Exoskeleton}$ in $\text{Arthropods}$ is termed:
image: [Image illustrating the molting process in an insect or crustacean]
explanation: $\text{Ecdysis}$, or $\text{Molting}$, is the process by which an $\text{Arthropod}$ $\text{Sheds}$ its $\text{Exoskeleton}$ to $\text{Allow}$ for $\text{Growth}$ and $\text{Change}$ in $\text{Body}$ $\text{Form}$.

text: The $\text{Organism}$ that $\text{Causes}$ $\text{Malaria}$ is a $\text{Protozoan}$ called:
image: [Microscopic image of Plasmodium falciparum in red blood cells]
explanation: $\text{Malaria}$ is caused by $\text{Protozoans}$ of the $\text{Genus}$ $\text{Plasmodium}$ ($	ext{P.}$ $\text{falciparum}$ being the most severe), transmitted by the female $\text{Anopheles}$ $\text{Mosquito}$.

text: Which part of the $\text{Nervous}$ $\text{System}$ is $\text{Responsible}$ for $\text{Voluntary}$ $\text{Actions}$?
image: [Diagram of the human brain highlighting the Cerebrum]
explanation: The $\text{Cerebrum}$ is the $\text{Largest}$ $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Brain}$ and is $\text{Responsible}$ for $\text{Higher}$-$\text{Order}$ $\text{Functions}$ like $\text{Thought}$, $\text{Memory}$, $\text{Language}$, and $\text{Voluntary}$ $\text{Movement}$.

text: The $\text{Layer}$ of the $\text{Earth}$ where $\text{Life}$ $\text{Exists}$ is known as the:
image: [Diagram illustrating the various components of the Biosphere]
explanation: The $\text{Biosphere}$ is the $\text{Portion}$ of the $\text{Earth}$ and $\text{Atmosphere}$ that $\text{Supports}$ $\text{Life}$, encompassing parts of the $\text{Lithosphere}$, $\text{Hydrosphere}$, and $\text{Atmosphere}$.

text: Which of the following hormones controls the $\text{Rate}$ of $\text{Metabolism}$ in the $\text{Body}$?
image: [Diagram showing the Thyroid gland and Thyroxine's role]
explanation: $\text{Thyroxine}$, produced by the $\text{Thyroid}$ $\text{Gland}$, is the $\text{Main}$ $\text{Hormone}$ that $\text{Regulates}$ the $\text{Basal}$ $\text{Metabolic}$ $\text{Rate}$ ($	ext{BMR}$) of the body.

text: The $\text{Primary}$ $\text{Site}$ of $\text{Gaseous}$ $\text{Exchange}$ in the $\text{Human}$ $\text{Lung}$ is the:
image: [Microscopic view of Alveoli surrounded by capillaries]
explanation: The $\text{Alveoli}$ are $\text{Tiny}$, $\text{Thin}$-$\text{Walled}$ $\text{Air}$ $\text{Sacs}$ surrounded by $\text{Capillaries}$ where $\text{Oxygen}$ diffuses $\text{Into}$ the $\text{Blood}$ and $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$ diffuses $\text{Out}$.

text: A $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Tissue}$ that is $\text{Dead}$ at $\text{Maturity}$ and provides $\text{Mechanical}$ $\text{Support}$ is the:
image: [Microscopic cross-section comparing Xylem and Phloem tissues]
explanation: $\text{Xylem}$ $\text{Vessels}$ and $\text{Tracheids}$ are $\text{Dead}$ $\text{Cells}$ at $\text{Maturity}$ and form $\text{Continuous}$ $\text{Tubes}$ for $\text{Water}$ $\text{Transport}$ and $\text{Structural}$ $\text{Support}$ (lignified walls).

text: The $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Cells}$ that are $\text{Involved}$ in $\text{Blood}$ $\text{Clotting}$ are the:
image: [Microscopic image showing Platelets aggregating at a site of injury]
explanation: $\text{Platelets}$ are $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Fragments}$ that $\text{Initiate}$ the $\text{Clotting}$ $\text{Process}$ by $\text{Aggregating}$ at the site of $\text{Injury}$ and releasing $\text{Clotting}$ $\text{Factors}$.

text: Which of the following $\text{Diseases}$ is $\text{NOT}$ caused by a $\text{Virus}$?
explanation: $\text{Tuberculosis}$ ($	ext{TB}$) is caused by the $\text{Bacterium}$ $\text{Mycobacterium}$ $\text{Tuberculosis}$. $\text{Measles}$, $\text{Polio}$, and $\text{AIDS}$ are all caused by $\text{Viruses}$.

text: The $\text{Main}$ $\text{Substance}$ that $\text{Gives}$ $\text{Rigidity}$ to the $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Walls}$ of $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Cells}$ is:
image: [Chemical structure of Cellulose]
explanation: $\text{Cellulose}$ is a $\text{Complex}$ $\text{Carbohydrate}$ and the $\text{Primary}$ $\text{Structural}$ $\text{Component}$ of $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Walls}$, providing $\text{Strength}$ and $\text{Rigidity}$. $\text{Lignin}$ is added to secondary walls for extra hardening.

text: The $\text{Movement}$ of $\text{Solvent}$ $\text{Molecules}$ across a $\text{Selectively}$ $\text{Permeable}$ $\text{Membrane}$ is known as:
image: [Diagram illustrating water molecules moving across a membrane during Osmosis]
explanation: $\text{Osmosis}$ is the $\text{Movement}$ of $\text{Water}$ ($	ext{Solvent}$) $\text{Molecules}$ from a $\text{Region}$ of $\text{Higher}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Potential}$ to a $\text{Region}$ of $\text{Lower}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Potential}$ across a $\text{Semipermeable}$ $\text{Membrane}$.

text: Which of these is $\text{NOT}$ a $\text{Sense}$ $\text{Organ}$?
explanation: The $\text{Spleen}$ is an $\text{Organ}$ of the $\text{Lymphatic}$ $\text{System}$ involved in $\text{Filtering}$ $\text{Blood}$ and $\text{Immune}$ $\text{Responses}$. The $\text{Eye}$, $\text{Skin}$, and $\text{Ear}$ contain $\text{Receptors}$ for $\text{Sensation}$.

text: The $\text{Hormone}$ that $\text{Regulates}$ the $\text{Amount}$ of $\text{Water}$ $\text{Reabsorbed}$ in the $\text{Kidneys}$ is:
image: [Diagram of the Nephron showing the effect of ADH on the collecting duct]
explanation: $\text{ADH}$ ($	ext{Vasopressin}$) is produced by the $\text{Hypothalamus}$ and released by the $\text{Pituitary}$. It $\text{Increases}$ the $\text{Permeability}$ of the $\text{Collecting}$ $\text{Ducts}$ in the $\text{Kidney}$, leading to $\text{More}$ $\text{Water}$ $\text{Reabsorption}$ and $\text{Concentrated}$ $\text{Urine}$.

text: The $\text{Microscopic}$ $\text{Unit}$ of $\text{Inheritance}$ located on a $\text{Chromosome}$ is called a:
image: [Diagram showing DNA structure, genes, and chromosomes]
explanation: A $\text{Gene}$ is a $\text{Segment}$ of $\text{DNA}$ located on a $\text{Chromosome}$ that $\text{Codes}$ for a $\text{Specific}$ $\text{Protein}$ or $\text{Functional}$ $\text{RNA}$, thereby determining a $\text{Trait}$.

text: Which of these $\text{Invertebrates}$ $\text{Possesses}$ a $\text{Water}$ $\text{Vascular}$ $\text{System}$?
image: [Diagram of a Starfish showing the water vascular system]
explanation: The $\text{Water}$ $\text{Vascular}$ $\text{System}$ is a $\text{Defining}$ $\text{Feature}$ of the $\text{Phylum}$ $\text{Echinodermata}$ (Starfish, Sea $\text{Urchins}$), used for $\text{Locomotion}$, $\text{Feeding}$, and $\text{Gas}$ $\text{Exchange}$.

text: The $\text{Part}$ of the $\text{Eye}$ that $\text{Changes}$ $\text{Size}$ to $\text{Control}$ the $\text{Amount}$ of $\text{Light}$ $\text{Entering}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the human eye focusing on the Iris and Pupil]
explanation: The $\text{Pupil}$ is the $\text{Opening}$ in the $\text{Centre}$ of the $\text{Iris}$. The $\text{Iris}$ $\text{Muscles}$ $\text{Contract}$ or $\text{Relax}$ to $\text{Adjust}$ the $\text{Diameter}$ of the $\text{Pupil}$, thus $\text{Regulating}$ $\text{Light}$ $\text{Intensity}$.

text: Which of the following $\text{Diseases}$ is $\text{Transmitted}$ by the $\text{Female}$ $\text{Anopheles}$ $\text{Mosquito}$?
explanation: The $\text{Female}$ $\text{Anopheles}$ $\text{Mosquito}$ serves as the $\text{Vector}$ for the $\text{Plasmodium}$ $\text{Protozoan}$ which causes $\text{Malaria}$.

text: In $\text{Respiration}$, the $\text{Energy}$ $\text{Released}$ from the $\text{Breakdown}$ of $\text{Glucose}$ is $\text{Stored}$ in the form of:
image: [Diagram of the ATP molecule structure and its energy storage]
explanation: $\text{ATP}$ is the $\text{Energy}$ $\text{Currency}$ of the $\text{Cell}$. The $\text{Energy}$ derived from $\text{Cellular}$ $\text{Respiration}$ is $\text{Used}$ to $\text{Synthesize}$ $\text{ATP}$ from $\text{ADP}$ and $\text{Phosphate}$.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Converting}$ $\text{Atmospheric}$ $\text{Nitrogen}$ into $\text{Nitrates}$ is called:
image: [Diagram illustrating the complete Nitrogen Cycle, highlighting Nitrogen Fixation and Nitrification]
explanation: $\text{Nitrogen}$ $\text{Fixation}$ is the process by which $\text{Atmospheric}$ $\text{Nitrogen}$ ($	ext{N}_2$) is $\text{Converted}$ into $\text{Ammonia}$ ($	ext{NH}_3$) or $\text{Nitrates}$ by $\text{Microorganisms}$ (like $\text{Rhizobium}$ or $\text{Azotobacter}$).

text: The $\text{Genetic}$ $\text{Make}$-$\text{up}$ of an $\text{Organism}$ is its:
explanation: The $\text{Genotype}$ is the $\text{Specific}$ $\text{Combination}$ of $\text{Alleles}$ (genetic information) inherited for a particular $\text{Trait}$, while the $\text{Phenotype}$ is the $\text{Observable}$ $\text{Expression}$ of that $\text{Trait}$.

text: The $\text{Site}$ where $\text{Carbohydrate}$ $\text{Digestion}$ $\text{Begins}$ in $\text{Humans}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the digestive system highlighting the oral cavity]
explanation: Carbohydrate $\text{Digestion}$ $\text{Begins}$ in the $\text{Mouth}$ with the action of $\text{Salivary}$ $\text{Amylase}$ (Ptyalin) on $\text{Starch}$.

text: Which of the following $\text{Plant}$ $\text{Hormones}$ is primarily $\text{Responsible}$ for $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Elongation}$ and $\text{Phototropism}$?
image: [Diagram illustrating the effect of Auxins on stem tip growth towards light]
explanation: $\text{Auxins}$ (especially $\text{IAA}$) are crucial for $\text{Apical}$ $\text{Dominance}$, $\text{Root}$ $\text{Initiation}$, and the differential $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Elongation}$ that underlies $\text{Phototropism}$ and $\text{Geotropism}$.

text: The $\text{Condition}$ where $\text{Two}$ $\text{Organisms}$ $\text{Benefit}$ $\text{Mutually}$ from $\text{Living}$ $\text{Together}$ is called:
image: [Diagram illustrating a mutualistic relationship (e.g., lichen or cleaner shrimp and fish)]
explanation: $\text{Mutualism}$ is a type of $\text{Symbiosis}$ where the $\text{Interaction}$ between $\text{Two}$ $\text{Different}$ $\text{Species}$ is $\text{Beneficial}$ to $\text{Both}$ $\text{Parties}$.

text: The $\text{Heart}$ $\text{Chamber}$ that $\text{Receives}$ $\text{Oxygenated}$ $\text{Blood}$ from the $\text{Lungs}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of the four chambers of the human heart]
explanation: The $\text{Left}$ $\text{Atrium}$ receives $\text{Oxygenated}$ $\text{Blood}$ from the $\text{Pulmonary}$ $\text{Veins}$ (from the $\text{Lungs}$) before pumping it to the $\text{Left}$ $\text{Ventricle}$.

text: Which of the following organisms belongs to the $\text{Class}$ $\text{Amphibia}$?
explanation: $\text{Amphibians}$ ($	ext{Frogs}$, $\text{Toads}$, $\text{Salamanders}$) typically undergo $\text{Metamorphosis}$ from an $\text{Aquatic}$ $\text{Larval}$ $\text{Stage}$ to a $\text{Terrestrial}$ $\text{Adult}$ $\text{Stage}$. $\text{Crocodile}$ and $\text{Lizard}$ are $\text{Reptiles}$.

text: The $\text{Specialized}$ $\text{Cells}$ in the $\text{Stomach}$ that $\text{Secrete}$ $\text{Hydrochloric}$ $\text{Acid}$ ($	ext{HCl}$) are the:
image: [Microscopic view of stomach lining cells, focusing on Parietal cells]
explanation: $\text{Parietal}$ $\text{Cells}$ (also known as $\text{Oxyntic}$ $\text{Cells}$) are responsible for the $\text{Secretion}$ of $\text{Hydrochloric}$ $\text{Acid}$ ($	ext{HCl}$) and $\text{Intrinsic}$ $\text{Factor}$ in the $\text{Stomach}$.

text: The $\text{Process}$ of $\text{Waste}$ $\text{Removal}$ from the $\text{Body}$ of an $\text{Organism}$ is termed:
explanation: $\text{Excretion}$ is the $\text{Removal}$ of $\text{Metabolic}$ $\text{Waste}$ $\text{Products}$ (like $\text{Urea}$, $\text{Carbon}$ $\text{Dioxide}$, $\text{Excess}$ $\text{Salts}$) from the body. $\text{Egestion}$ is the $\text{Removal}$ of $\text{Undigested}$ $\text{Food}$ (faeces).

text: The $\text{Structure}$ that $\text{Transports}$ $\text{Synthesized}$ $\text{Food}$ from the $\text{Leaves}$ to $\text{Other}$ $\text{Parts}$ of the $\text{Plant}$ is the:
image: [Diagram of a plant stem cross-section highlighting Xylem and Phloem]
explanation: The $\text{Phloem}$ tissue is responsible for $\text{Translocation}$, the $\text{Transport}$ of $\text{Soluble}$ $\text{Organic}$ $\text{Food}$ $\text{Products}$ (mainly $\text{Sucrose}$) from the $\text{Leaves}$ ($	ext{Source}$) to $\text{Growth}$ and $\text{Storage}$ $\text{Areas}$ ($	ext{Sinks}$).

text: Which of the following $\text{Involves}$ $\text{Genetic}$ $\text{Recombination}$?
image: [Diagram illustrating Crossing Over during Prophase I of Meiosis]
explanation: $\text{Meiosis}$ ($	ext{Reduction}$ $\text{Division}$) is the process that $\text{Produces}$ $\text{Gametes}$. It $\text{Includes}$ $\text{Crossing}$ $\text{Over}$ (Prophase $\text{I}$) and $\text{Independent}$ $\text{Assortment}$, which $\text{Lead}$ to $\text{Genetic}$ $\text{Recombination}$ and $\text{Variation}$.

text: The $\text{Long}$-$\text{Term}$ $\text{Effect}$ of $\text{Desertification}$ is:
image: [Satellite image showing advanced desertification (soil degradation and barren land)]
explanation: $\text{Desertification}$ is the $\text{Process}$ by which $\text{Fertile}$ $\text{Land}$ becomes $\text{Desert}$. Its main $\text{Long}$-$\text{Term}$ $\text{Effect}$ is the $\text{Irreversible}$ $\text{Loss}$ of $\text{Productive}$ $\text{Agricultural}$ ($	ext{Arable}$) $\text{Land}$.

text: The $\text{Major}$ $\text{Constituent}$ of the $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Membrane}$ is:
image: [Diagram of the fluid mosaic model of the cell membrane]
explanation: The $\text{Cell}$ $\text{Membrane}$ is structured as a $\text{Fluid}$ $\text{Mosaic}$ of a $\text{Phospholipid}$ $\text{Bilayer}$ with $\text{Various}$ $\text{Proteins}$ embedded in or attached to it.

text: A $\text{Type}$ of $\text{Budding}$ that $\text{Occurs}$ in $\text{Yeast}$ is an example of:
image: [Microscopic image of Yeast cells undergoing budding]
explanation: $\text{Budding}$ in $\text{Yeast}$ involves the $\text{Formation}$ of a $\text{Small}$ $\text{Outgrowth}$ ($	ext{Bud}$) that $\text{Detaches}$ from the $\text{Parent}$ $\text{Cell}$ and $\text{Grows}$ into a $\text{New}$ $\text{Organism}$. This does $\text{Not}$ involve the $\text{Fusion}$ of $\text{Gametes}$.

text: The $\text{Instrument}$ $\text{Used}$ to $\text{Measure}$ $\text{Relative}$ $\text{Humidity}$ is the:
explanation: A $\text{Hygrometer}$ is an $\text{Instrument}$ $\text{Used}$ for $\text{Measuring}$ the $\text{Amount}$ of $\text{Water}$ $\text{Vapour}$ in the $\text{Atmosphere}$ ($	ext{Humidity}$). An $\text{Anemometer}$ measures $\text{Wind}$ $\text{Speed}$.

text: The $\text{Primary}$ $\text{Function}$ of the $\text{Large}$ $\text{Intestine}$ in $\text{Humans}$ is:
image: [Diagram of the human large intestine]
explanation: While the $\text{Small}$ $\text{Intestine}$ is the $\text{Main}$ $\text{Site}$ for $\text{Nutrient}$ $\text{Absorption}$, the $\text{Large}$ $\text{Intestine}$ is $\text{Primarily}$ $\text{Responsible}$ for $\text{Reabsorbing}$ $\text{Water}$ and $\text{Ions}$ from the $\text{Undigested}$ $\text{Food}$ $\text{Residue}$, $\text{Forming}$ $\text{Faeces}$.
